evidence_class: Mocked Redis (fakeredis), a fake clock and a fake Pod source that emits list, watch, expired cursor and deletion events; no Kubernetes API, node autoscaler or EC2 call was made.
interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.kubernetes.watch: OWNER_LABEL and EXECUTION_LABEL, owner_for(slug) as the plan independent owner value, labels(owner, execution_id), PodSource with list_pods, watch_pods, read_pod and delete_pod under a uid precondition
PodView keys observed Pods by uid and relists on an expired cursor, a connection error or a timeout
Reconciler.plan classifies managed orphan, missing pod, foreign, ambiguous and terminating Pods; cleanup is a constructor switch independent of matching

Controller(pods=PodView, orphan_cleanup=bool): acquire reconciles after operation recovery and before admission opens; reconcile() plans from the current kubernetes execution occupants and the Pod view, deletes an orphan only when a fresh read still equals the observed Pod and the lease still holds, and records the class counts
Controller.controller_orphans_by_class() reads the latest counts from the per swarm controller-orphans hash

supported_versions.redis: Hashes only; the counts hash is observational
supported_versions.kubernetes: Any API that supports label selector list, resource version watch with 410 expiry and delete preconditions on uid; no client is wired yet
supported_versions.compatibility: A Controller without a Pod view reconciles nothing and behaves exactly as SV2-CTL-03; the local herdr path is unchanged

authority: Every reconcile and every delete re-checks the scoped controller grant and the lease through the controller authority check. The owner label value derives from the swarm slug, never from a Pod name or display label. A Pod lacking the owner label is never listed; a Pod with another owner, an empty execution id or a twin for one execution is quarantined, never deleted.

states.observed: Cases A, B and C each passed twice from independent fake Redis servers and Pod sources with identical outputs. Controller and watch tests passed, 45 in total.
states.accepted: A restarted controller matches the existing managed Pod, deletes only the managed orphan and launches nothing; unlabelled lookalikes, foreign owners and ambiguous Pods leave protected state unchanged; an expired cursor relists, and a delayed deletion of an old incarnation leaves the newer Pod matched.
states.committed: Code and fixture inputs are at tested_commit.
states.externally_verified: None: no Kubernetes Pod source is wired and no live G3 deployment was exercised.

validation.lint: ruff check passed on changed Python files
validation.format: ruff format check passed on changed Python files
validation.mutation: Pending the pull request CI run

rollback_rehearsal.action: Construct the controller with orphan_cleanup False: status matching and missing pod detection continue while no Pod is deleted.
rollback_rehearsal.authoritative_objects: The execution journal (executions hash, controller intents, runtime operations) and the Kubernetes Pods themselves; the controller-orphans counts hash is observational and safe to discard.
rollback_rehearsal.proof: Case C restarts a controller with cleanup disabled over the same store after a managed orphan appears: the orphan survives, the newer incarnation stays matched and no launch happens.

remaining_limitations: No Kubernetes API Pod source exists yet; a later runtime package must implement PodSource over list, watch and delete with a uid precondition.
Missing pod executions are reported, not relaunched; relaunch stays with the tick and admission path.
Quarantined Pods are counted and returned on the plan but not persisted for operator review.
controller_orphans_by_class is a Redis hash read through a method; no telemetry exporter emits it yet.
Mutation qualification is pending the pull request CI run.
